adjudication.rationale: The handler does perform a non-atomic read-then-write check (it reads existing attendees via `findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`, computes `uniqueGuests`, then later does `booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})`), so concurrent calls could bypass the in-memory duplicate filtering. However, the proposed finding specifically claims there is "no DB-level uniqueness constraint or transaction" and that duplicates will be inserted. The diff does not show the Prisma schema / DB constraints for attendees (e.g., a unique index on `(bookingId, email)`), nor any `skipDuplicates` or explicit transaction usage. Without seeing the DB constraints, it is not verifiable from this diff that duplicates can actually be inserted (a DB constraint could instead cause one call to fail).
